title: Review B1 (T-0016): [[executors]] table, pick_executor, quota-group cooldowns
spec: Adversarial review of the T-0016 diff against its acceptance criteria (skill adversarial-review). Executed by claude:opus on account A via fallback; you must be a different model on the other account. Focus: (1) pick_executor filters: enabled, role, complexity range, cooling, max_parallel, daily budget — any path that returns a disabled or out-of-range executor? (2) cooldown_executor cools every enabled member of the quota_group, and only that group. (3) pool_state.json round trip: missing "executors" key on old state files must not crash; day rollover resets day_tasks. (4) codex_available() semantics preserved for existing callers (executor.start, mcp.status, cli). (5) TOML parses with tomllib; no key typos between pool.toml and the dataclass. (6) tests actually assert the behaviours rather than mirroring the implementation. Return ONLY the review JSON: {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[{"path":"","line":0,"issue":"","severity":"low|med|high"}]}. Output under 3,000 chars.
acceptance: verdict approve or request_changes with line-anchored comments
each high-severity comment names a concrete failing input

comments.issue: codex_available() now returns True if ANY enabled executor has headroom, probed at a hardcoded complexity=1 rather than the real task complexity, and only checks ex.provider=="codex" (true for every row). executor.py:81 is unchanged and always dispatches the actual `codex exec -m <model>` using pool.cfg['codex']['model'] (astra), ignoring which executor pick_executor found. Concrete failure: astra.running=2 (== its max_parallel=2) and astra.day_tasks=40 (== its daily_budget_tasks), while luna/terra/sol sit idle. A complexity=8 task (only astra's 1-10 band covers it) calls codex_available() -> pick_executor('execute',1) matches luna (band 1-6 includes the probe value 1) and returns it, so codex_available() reports True even though astra itself is exhausted and no idle row actually supports complexity 8. executor.py's start() then launches a 3rd concurrent `codex exec -m gpt-6-astra`, busting astra's own max_parallel and daily_budget_tasks caps -- the exact limits [[executors]] exists to enforce. None of the new tests exercise codex_available() with one row exhausted and another free, so this ships uncaught.

_sync_legacy_codex folds self.codex.running/day_tasks into the matched executor row with max() only, never assigning down. executor.py builds a fresh Pool() per call (start()/reply() each do `pool = Pool()`) and each call's finally-block save() persists that instance's own in-memory (possibly stale) executors dict. If task A's Pool() and task B's Pool() overlap, whichever saves last can clobber the other's running/day_tasks count with a stale snapshot, and nothing ever recomputes the executor row from scratch to correct it -- so astra's tracked running/day_tasks can drift permanently away from the true self.codex value after a handful of overlapping calls.
